chapter_name: Change and Development in Industrial Society
learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how work is organized in modern India, the harsh realities of the informal sector, and how liberalization changed the way we work!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The formal sector has regular salaries, pensions, and job security, but employs a tiny fraction of Indians. Over 90% work in the informal sector (vendors, daily wagers) with no social security.
Karl Marx's concept where factory workers doing repetitive tasks (like tightening a single bolt all day) feel disconnected from the final product, their own skills, and their fellow workers.
Since 1991, India has opened its economy. This created new jobs like BPOs and IT, but also led to 'contractualisation', where companies hire temporary workers to easily fire them and save money.
Workers organizing to demand better pay and conditions. A massive example is the 1982 Bombay Textile Strike, which eventually led to the closure of many mills.

fun_activity.title: 👷 Sector Spotter
fun_activity.instructions: Make a list of 5 working adults you know (parents, neighbors, the local chaiwala, the school guard). Categorize their jobs into 'Formal' or 'Informal' based on whether they have a written contract and pension.

exam_tips: 📌 Emphasize that India's industrialization is unique because the vast majority of our workforce remains in the unorganized/informal sector.
📌 Understand 'Scientific Management' (Taylorism): breaking down work into tiny, timed tasks to maximize factory efficiency, often treating humans like machines.
📌 Home-based work (like rolling beedis or assembling toys) is a massive part of the informal economy, largely done by women.
quick_recap: ⭐ Industrialization leads to a finer division of labor, where people do highly specialized tasks.
⭐ Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) has changed the retail landscape, bringing in multinational corporations and malls.
⭐ Working conditions in the informal sector often completely bypass government labor laws.
